 November 16, 2026 | Men's Basketball
 Tennessee Notes MSU Notes Watch (ESPN2) Listen Live Live Stats Share: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. – The Tennessee men's basketball team is set to continue the 2026-27 season Tuesday as it hosts the No. 2/3 Michigan State Spartans. Tipoff is set for 9 p.m. ET. 
 GAMEDAY TIMES & BROADCAST INFO
 Opponent:  Michigan State Spartans 
 Tipoff:  Tuesday, Nov. 17 | 9 p.m. ET
 Venue:   Food City Center 
 Watch Online:  ESPN2 
 Online:   Listen Live |  Live Stats

 Roster Schedule   Game Notes

 Roster Schedule   Game Notes 
 THE LATEST FROM THE VOLS
 Vols Ranked #14 in Both Polls #11/9 Vols Improve to 3-0 with 83-78 Win over Tennessee State #11/9 Vols Upend Radford, 70-47, Behind Defensive Dominance Vols Place #11/9 Nationally After First Week of Games #8/9 Vols Defeat Wofford, 90-59, in Season Opener 
Fans can watch Tuesday's game on ESPN2 and stream the game on WatchESPN.com and the ESPN app. Tom Hart (play-by-play) and Jimmy Dykes (color) will have the call.
Fans state-wide can tune in to their local Vol Network radio affiliate to hear Voice of the Vols Mike Keith and analyst Chris Lofton depict the action.
Tennessee is coming off a 3-0 start to the season, with wins over Wofford, Radford and Tennessee State in Food City Center.
 THE MATCHUP 
• The only official matchup in the last 30 years came on 3/28/10, with #13 Michigan State claiming a 70-69 Elite Eight triumph over #15 Tennessee in St. Louis.
• Prior to that, the schools met in back-to-back years three separate times. Those games were 1/23/39 and 1/6/40, 12/30/70 and 12/18/71, and 12/21/93 and 12/20/94.
• Rick Barnes and Tom Izzo also met in the Elite Eight on 3/30/03, with #5 Texas winning, 85-76, in San Antonio.
• The teams' last meeting was an exhibition contest on 10/29/23, which #9/10 Tennessee won, 89- 88, at #4 Michigan State behind 28 points from Dalton Knecht.
• The Vols are 36-44 against the Big Ten's current members. Barnes is 43-42, including 10-10 at UT.
• After a 27-8 (15-5) campaign that included a Sweet 16 berth, the Spartans placed second in the Big Ten preseason poll.
• Redshirt junior guard Jeremy Fears Jr., the Big Ten Preseason Player of the Year, leads Michigan State with 16.8 ppg and a nationbest 10.0 apg this season.
 NEWS & NOTES 
• Rick Barnes (30) and Tom Izzo (28) rank first and second among active head coaches in DI NCAA Tournament bids.
• The Volunteers are the only team to play in the Sweet 16 in each of the last four years and in the Elite Eight in each of the past three.
• Last year, Tennessee logged, per CBS, the sixth instance of an SEC team reaching the Sweet 16 at least four years in a row, since the field grew to 32 in 1975.
• UT is, according to Stats Perform, one of three SEC schools—five instances—to make the Elite Eight at least three years in a row, since the tournament expanded to 16 teams in 1951. The others are Kentucky (2010-12, 1995-99, 1956- 58) and Florida (2011-14).
• Rick Barnes ' 864 wins are second among active DI coaches and No. 10 all-time (min. 10 years in DI). That also ties him with Bob Huggins for ninth in DI-only wins.
• Barnes is one game away from becoming the fourth head coach with 1,300 games at the DI level. The others are Mike Krzyzewski, Jim Boeheim and Cliff Ellis.
• The Volunteers' +12.6 rebounding margin in 2025-26 was the thirdbest of the last 30 years (1996- 2026), according to Stats Perform.
• Tennesse sports an 8-3 record in its last 11 games versus AP top-11 teams, dating to 2/1/25, including a 4-1 tally last year. All three losses are to teams that made the NCAA final, two of which won the title.
• UT is 11-1 at home against AP top11 opponents under Rick Barnes , with 10 straight wins dating to 3/2/19. The Vols are 9-1 versus the top 10 and 8-0 against the top six.
• Tennessee has won 47 consecutive non-conference home contests. The streak spans seven seasons, dating to a win over Colorado on 12/8/20 in the 2020-21 opener. It is DI's third-longest active mark.
• The Vols' 229 wins the last 10 seasons (2017-26) rank eighth in DI. Only Houston (276), Gonzaga (272), Duke (258), Kansas (239), Purdue (238), Arizona (233) and Saint Mary's (230) possess more. Auburn (226) and Liberty (226) complete the top 10. In addition, UT is also eighth over the last six seasons (2021-27) with 137 wins.
 WINNING WAYS 
• Over the last 10 seasons (2017-27), Tennessee (229- 86; .727) paces all SEC schools in total victories, overall winning percentage and postseason victories (27). In that span, UT has three SEC titles (2018 and 2024 regular seasons, 2022 tournament).
• In that same period, the Volunteers are one of two SEC teams with even 215-plus wins and/or a winning percentage above .685, alongside Auburn (226-88; .720), which ranks second in both areas.
• Over SEC play across the same span, Tennessee (109-52; .677) is first in both league victories and league winning percentage. The only other schools at even 100-plus wins and/or a .620 clip are Kentucky (107-54; .665), Alabama (104-58; .642) and Auburn (103-59; .636).
• In just the last six seasons (2021-27), the Vols own a 137-48 (.741) overall record. That is good for the most total wins and the best winning percentage in the SEC, far ahead of Auburn (.725; 132-50) and Alabama (.721; 132-51).
• In that time, Tennessee (62-28; .689) is second in league victories and league winning percentage, behind only Alabama (64-26; .711).
 RACKING UP RANKED VICTORIES... 
• TOP 25: Across the past six years (2021-27), the Volunteers' 36 AP top-25 wins co-lead DI, alongside Connecticut (36). Only Arizona (35), Alabama (33), Kansas (33), Iowa State (30), Purdue (30) and Duke (29) are even at 28-plus.
• TOP 20: Tennessee co-leads the nation with 32 AP top-20 triumphs over that span, tying Connecticut (32). Just Arizona (29), Kansas (28), Alabama (27), Duke (24) and Purdue (24) are even at 24-plus.
• TOP 15: The Vols lead the country with 26 AP top-15 wins in those five years. Kansas (25), Arizona (24), Alabama (20), Connecticut (20), Iowa State (19) and Purdue (19) are the lone others at even 19-plus.
• TOP 10: Since 2021-22, UT is co-second in DI with 15 AP top-10 wins, trailing just Arizona (16), while tying Iowa State (15) and Kansas (15). Only Connecticut (14), Purdue (13), Alabama (12), Florida (12), Kentucky (11), Texas Tech (11) and Wisconsin (11) are at even 11-plus.
• TOP FIVE: In the same six-year period, the Volunteers are second in DI with eight AP top-five victories, behind only Arizona (10). Alabama (seven), Florida (seven), Iowa State (seven) and Kansas (six) are the only others with even six-plus.
• TOP THREE: UT is co-second in DI, alongside Florida and Iowa State, with five AP top-three decisions in those six years, trailing just Arizona (seven). Only Alabama, Duke, Texas Tech and Wisconsin are even at four.
 ...AND DOING SO EFFICIENTLY 
• Tennessee, at 36-26 (.581), has the SEC's best record versus AP top-25 foes over the last six seasons (2021-27). Florida (27-23; .540) places second, while no one else has a figure over .520.
• The Volunteers are 32-19 (.627) against AP top-20 teams in that span, 13 games over the .500 mark. Auburn (20-19; .513) is a distant second among SEC schools, with no others above even a .500 tally.
• Tennessee is 26-14 (.650) versus AP top-15 foes in that time. Auburn (15-15; .500) is a far second in the SEC, as the only other team above even a .475 clip.
• At 15-10 (.600), the Vols have the best record in the SEC against AP top-10 foes over those six seasons. The only other SEC team above even a .410 figure is distant second-place Florida (12-12; .500).
• With an 8-8 (.500) ledger, Tennessee has the second-best record in the SEC versus AP top-five teams in that stretch, barely trailing only Florida (7- 6; .538). No other team owns a clip above even .365.
• Even with its excellent winning percentage, UT has played the third-most games (62) against AP top25 foes of any DI team the last six years (2021-27). The Vols trail only Texas (65) and Alabama (64), with Kansas (60) the lone other school at 60-plus.
 HOLDING SERVE, HISTORICALLY 
• The Volunteers have won 47 non-conference home games in a row, dating to the to the 2020-21 season opener (12/8/20). They finished each of the past six years undefeated at home in non-conference play.
• Per Elias Sports Bureau, that 47-game streak is the longest in program history. The prior top tally of 43 came from 12/7/40 to 12/10/49.
• The Vols' 47-game regular season non-conference home winning streak is third-best in DI. That trails only Baylor (55) and Texas Tech (50). The lone others above even 40 are Akron (44), Iowa State (44) and Providence (42).
• The only other school with 47-plus such wins and no losses over the past seven years (2020-27) is Texas Tech (50-0). Just five additional programs own a mark above even 10-0: Baylor (46-0), Providence (40-0), Akron (34-0), Southern (15-0) and Prairie View A&M (12-0).
• During its streak, Tennessee owns victories over teams such as Arizona, Cincinnati, Colorado, Illinois, Kansas, Louisville, Syracuse and Texas. Related News
